turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Bloods are in, so we'll keep this tight. What brought you in today.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, nothing's wrong, doc. I'm only here for the kidney numbers they phoned about.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dad, don't start. You've been flat on the couch every afternoon.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): She's dramatic. I feel like a wet rag after the garden, that's all. I've overdone it. I'm not breathless, I walk to the shop fine.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tired, then. Any fever?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. Throat's fine.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bowels. Any diarrhoea or constipation?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Bowels are fine.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight. Lost any?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, maybe. Belt's a notch looser. I don't weigh myself and I couldn't tell you when. I'm not fading away, hey.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Creatinine is one seven two. eGFR thirty four. Your chronic kidney disease has slipped, last eGFR was forty one. Still taking the ramipril?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, the rampiril. Five mg, every morning. I take it.
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not every morning. Tuesday and yesterday were still in the pill box. I checked.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, one or two, shame. Mostly I take it. Don't make a case.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the five milligrams every morning, for the blood pressure and the kidneys. Do not stop the ramipril.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): And the sugar one, glyclazide, eighty milligrams in the morning. The metformin I stopped in March. Kidney clinic said leave it.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Type two diabetes, so the gliclazide stays. Correct that you stopped the metformin. Did you ever start the vitamin D I scripted?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Didn't collect it. Not taking something I don't need.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Knees. What painkiller are you on?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprofin from the Clicks. Two hundred milligram ones. Two a day, sometimes three, when the knees ache. Sister said not to. Ag, it's nothing, just from the shop.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Most days, for weeks. And tell him about your feet.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): My feet feel dead, both of them, like I'm walking on sand. It's just the cold, not a thing. Umm, couldn't say when it started, long time.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both feet numb. Ankles, I'm looking. No swelling.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, no swelling. And I'm not short of... ag, ok, the stairs, I have to stop halfway, proper puffing. Only the stairs, flat ground I'm fine.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He stops on our stairs too. I can't hear myself think when he puts the rugby on, but that's not why we're here.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the ibuprofen today. With the ramipril it is the likely reason the creatinine climbed, working impression, not proven. Paracetamol one gram, up to three times a day, for the knees. Nothing else from the pharmacy.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol is useless. But ja, I'll leave the ibuprofin.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll take the box out the cupboard at home. He stays with me, since last year.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure today is 146 over 84. Pulse 76. Repeat kidney bloods in two weeks, that's booked at the lab. See me here the Thursday after those bloods.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Can I still braai on Saturday. That's the important bit.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Braai is fine. Go easy on the salt. If the puffing gets worse before the Thursday, come in sooner. We're done.

spec.situation: Older diabetic with kidney disease on review; creatinine and eGFR read aloud; takes ibuprofen from a shop against advice; ramipril continued, painkiller advice changed.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Drug, dose, frequency, indication stated; 'currently_used' is uncertain due missed doses.
bad.text: ramipril (dose=5 mg, frequency=once daily, indication=blood pressure and kidneys, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Negative finding: patient denied sore throat ('Throat's fine').
Kidney function results were specifically stated: creatinine 172 and eGFR 34, with prior eGFR 41 indicating CKD has worsened.
Ramipril adherence concern is stronger than recorded: family member reported missed doses on Tuesday and yesterday, and patient admitted missing 'one or two'.
Metformin discontinuation timing/reason: patient stopped metformin in March because the kidney clinic told him to leave it, and doctor confirmed this was correct.
Vitamin D was prescribed previously but never started because the patient did not collect it.
Ibuprofen frequency is recorded incorrectly: patient takes 200 mg tablets, two a day and sometimes three, most days for weeks, not strictly two to three times daily.
Exertional dyspnoea detail: patient denied breathlessness on flat ground/walking to the shop and is only short of breath on stairs, needing to stop halfway.
Paracetamol effectiveness concern: patient said paracetamol is useless, although agreed to stop ibuprofen.
